mechanism_narrative: A higher level of quarterly GDP (GDPC1) indicates stronger economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where GDPC1 is above its 3-year rolling median, or the rank correlation between GDPC1 and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuation multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4.5%) signals a restrictive monetary policy combined with a weak labor market, indicating elevated recession risk and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND UNRATE > 4.5%, or the rank correlation between the interaction term and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by a 0.5% or greater rise in FEDFUNDS over a 3-month period), the market experiences increased risk aversion and reduced liquidity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 3 months, or the rank correlation between the regime condition and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a weak labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5%, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high housing starts (HOUST > 1350 thousand units) and high industrial production (INDPRO > 100.5) signals strong economic demand and supply, indicating robust growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1350 AND INDPRO > 100.5, or the rank correlation between the interaction term and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above its 3-year rolling median, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion (defined by housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1350 thousand units and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 700,000 million dollars), the economy is near full capacity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to strong consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1350 AND RSAFS > 700000, or the rank correlation between the regime condition and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
